name: Fatima Nazreen Khan
missingPieces: Task 3 did not clearly conclude that Artefact A is unrecoverable, and capstone D2 Artefact 04 claimed a wordlist crack instead of proving the captured token was tampered.
feedback: You showed a solid grasp of the JWT alg:none failure, the hash rotation order, and the board-level point that keys and trust controls matter more than algorithm names. The biggest issue is the honesty trap in capstone Artefact 04: the captured HS256 token was tampered, so the correct work was to recover the real secret from leaked source, prove the captured signature fails, and explain why it is not a normal hashcat or rockyou crack. Task 3 also needed a clearer final statement that Artefact A cannot be recovered from the provided text, rather than only saying the key was not easy to find. Your capstone tables and controls are understandable, but some standards are loose and the layered memo section does not give the exact final plaintext. Next time, treat any forced crack or too-clean plaintext as something to verify against the evidence before reporting it as solved.

name: Lucky Ogwuazor
missingPieces: No Task 3 write-up was submitted, and capstone D2 omitted Artefact 04.
feedback: Your Task 6 and Task 7 write-ups are strong, especially the hash prefix reasoning and the distinction between alg:none acceptance and trusting a role claim. The report loses a large block because Task 3 is missing entirely, so none of the three-string analysis can be credited. In the capstone, D2 also omits Artefact 04, which required showing that the captured HS256 token was tampered, recovering the real source secret, and explaining why a wordlist crack is not the right answer. Your board brief is concise and useful, and D3 gives five controls that mostly map to the failures, but the appendix needs exact plaintext and every required artefact. For future submissions, use the checklist from the brief as a hard completion test before you submit.
